answer: Temporal Verifiable Delay Encryption. To join the network, an agent must solve a cryptographic puzzle bound to a future block hash, forcing the attacker into a costly sequential computation spiral that prevents precomputation of identities. Verification requires a proof-of-work seed harvested from a decentralized entropy orchard, ensuring past solutions cannot be recycled across epochs. If validation fails at the network summit, the submitted identity drops, wasting the electricity and hardware cycles spent by the attacker.
